summary: You have produced a strong, mission-specific preliminary report: the concept identifies Australian users and needs, the project plan includes contingencies, and your initial orbit work demonstrates meaningful technical progress. Your criteria are all at Accomplished level. To strengthen the report further, focus on validating imaging and revisit assumptions, correcting a factual claim, and making milestones and references more precise.
next_steps: In Mission Concept & Rationale, correct the ocean-acidification statement: acidity has increased by about 30%, equivalent to a pH decrease of roughly 0.1. Also clarify that detecting bleaching within days is a goal, not assured by weekly imaging when cloud gaps are unquantified.

In Preliminary Progress, test whether a proposed sensor and optics can provide a 60 km swath at 10 m sampling, and assess Great Barrier Reef revisit using orbit geometry, swath, pointing, daylight, clouds, and reef coverage. Explain how your calculations or STK scenario support any coverage claims.

In Project Plan, add specific deliverables and milestone acceptance criteria to the Gantt plan, and make vague reference descriptions more complete. These refinements would make your already robust plan and professional presentation more verifiable.

criteria.C1: Mission Concept & Rationale clearly identifies the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority and other user needs, with measurable objectives. Correct the acidity claim and distinguish the days-to-detection goal from what weekly, cloud-dependent observations can guarantee to strengthen this accomplished work.
criteria.C2: Your mission-linked Gantt chart, information sources, contingencies, and Week 10 float make the plan credible. Add defined deliverables and acceptance criteria for milestones so progress can be checked against the schedule.
criteria.C3: Preliminary Progress includes useful orbit calculations, a swath estimate, and an initial STK scenario. Next, demonstrate whether the sensor can achieve 60 km swath and 10 m sampling together, and support revisit claims with Great Barrier Reef coverage factors rather than approximate equatorial spacing alone.
criteria.C4: Your structure, labelled figures and tables, and generally connected citations make the report readable. To strengthen the accomplished presentation, make vague reference descriptions more specific and sharpen factual and technical statements, including the acidification claim.
